children: Crude oil and refined product futures prices had backed off earlier highs but were still seeing increases Monday as markets reacted to the flare-up in fighting between the United States and Iran.

Crude prices were more than $1/bbl off overnight highs at 11:15 a.m. ET, with the NYMEX October West Texas Intermediate contract ahead by $1.73 to $85.13/bbl while November prices were trading up $1.75 to $83.58/bbl.
The November ICE Brent crude contract was $2.18 ahead to $90.28/bbl in light trade in its last session in the front-month position, while the more-active
December contract was seeing gains of $1.99 to $88.11/bbl.

Most activity in refined products was also focused on the next-month contracts as September contracts approached expiration. September ULSD futures were rising by 14.72cts to $4.5039/gal, about 3.5ct lower than earlier highs.

October ULSD was 16.08cts higher to $4.4098/gal. RBOB futures were mixed, with the September contract falling by 2.31cts in light trade to $3.4668/gal while October futures were moving up by 1.37cts to $3.0639/gal.

Prices are rising after the U.S. and Iran traded military attacks over the weekend, with the U.S. striking rocket launchers it said were being deployed to sow mines in the waters around the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said it responded by launching strikes on U.S. bases in the region.
The fighting is the first since July and raises the specter of a new re-escalation in the conflict and the further disruption of energy shipments from the region.

"The United States appears to be trying to maintain a balance: allowing oil to continue flowing through the strait as quickly as possible while protecting tankers, without being dragged into broad escalation in the immediate short term," said Samer Hasn, senior market analyst at XS.com. "An informal strategic truce appears likely over the next few months, despite recurring skirmishes."
Over the weekend, the Trump administration said it had reached a deal to develop Venezuelan oil reserves, but it's unclear what impact that is having on markets Monday.
